nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Turns any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into a persistent, queryable knowledge graph with an honest EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS audit trail; community detection surfaces cross-document connections users would not think to ask about.

nodes.label: Structural AST Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free; runs in parallel with LLM semantic extraction because the two operate on different file types, saving 5-15s on large corpora.

nodes.label: Parallel Semantic Extraction Subagents
nodes.rationale: Agent tool dispatch is mandatory because reading files one-by-one is 5-10x slower; all subagents must be dispatched in a single message to actually run in parallel, and must be general-purpose (not Explore) so they can write chunk files to disk.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Checked before dispatching any subagents so already-extracted files cost zero tokens on re-runs.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge, never hide cohesion scores, always show token cost; uncertain relationships are marked AMBIGUOUS rather than omitted, preserving an honest audit trail.

nodes.label: Discrete Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: Models follow discrete rubrics better than continuous ranges; production data showed a bimodal collapse (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+), so INFERRED edges must pick one of five fixed values (0.55-0.95) and never default to 0.5.

nodes.label: Graph Query / Path / Explain Traversal
nodes.rationale: BFS for broad 'what is X connected to' context, DFS for tracing a specific dependency chain; answers must use only what the graph contains, citing source_location, to avoid hallucinated edges.

nodes.label: Save-Result Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Each query answer is saved back into the graph so the next --update extracts the Q&A as a node, improving future queries.

nodes.label: Incremental Update (--update)
nodes.rationale: Only re-extracts changed files to save tokens; code-only changes skip LLM semantic extraction entirely; changed-file nodes are pruned before merge to avoid collapsing same-named symbols across files (#1178); build_merge preserves edge direction (#801).

nodes.label: Whisper Video/Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: A domain-hint prompt composed from god-node labels is passed to Whisper as the initial prompt, improving transcription accuracy with no separate API call.

nodes.label: Watch Mode Auto-Rebuild (--watch)
nodes.rationale: Code-only changes rebuild via AST with no LLM; doc/paper/image changes only set a needs_update flag because they require paid LLM re-extraction. Debounce waits for file activity to stop so a wave of parallel agent writes triggers one rebuild, not one per file.

nodes.label: GitHub Clone and Cross-Repo Merge
nodes.rationale: Monorepo subfolders must use the CLI directly (graphify extract) because the skill pipeline writes all output to one graphify-out/ dir and separate runs would clobber it; each merged node carries a repo attribute for origin filtering.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Auto-Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit with no background process; only code changes are handled by the hook because doc/image changes need LLM re-extraction via manual --update.

nodes.label: Project Pivot (2026-04-24)
nodes.rationale: Benban-scale soiling/energy/TEC-vs-VCR calculations are no longer the core deliverable; they are reframed as feasibility evidence inside the methodology chapter, while the autonomous robot design becomes the primary graduation-project deliverable.

nodes.label: Autonomous TEC-Based PV-Cleaning Robot
nodes.rationale: Self-generates distilled cleaning water via thermoelectric cooling and autonomously cleans PV panels, eliminating external water supply in arid Egyptian conditions (RH 25-55%, T_amb 25-42 C).

nodes.label: Benban TEC Feasibility Evidence
nodes.rationale: Prior Benban (1.65 GWp) analyses are kept as feasibility validation that TEC atmospheric water harvesting works in arid Egyptian climate, justifying the robot design rather than serving as the deliverable.

nodes.label: Three Deployment Scales (Commercial / Residential / Street-Lamp PV)
nodes.rationale: Commercial rooftops 50-500 kWp, residential 3-20 kWp, street-lamp 100-400 Wp per pole; industrial scale is a stretch target. Three chassis variants: rooftop crawler, residential light crawler, pole-mounted unit.

nodes.label: Tables 6.1 vs 6.2 Energy Recovery Contradiction
nodes.rationale: Table 6.2 implies recovery of ~94% of annual yield, physically impossible; Table 6.1's 3.5% mean soiling-loss model is self-consistent, so 6.2 must be regenerated from the same model and tariff (Scale B payback ~9 years, not 1.9).

nodes.label: TEC Specific Energy Consumption Optimism (0.927 vs 2.8-12 kWh/L)
nodes.rationale: Derived SEC is 3-10x more optimistic than the cited literature; likely error is the air-side mass balance (8.4 m3/h assumed vs typical 2-4 m3/h for a 40x40 mm cold plate with a 60 mm fan); recompute with a datasheet fan curve and eta_c 0.30-0.60.
nodes.norm_label: tec specific energy consumption optimism (0.927 vs 2.8-12 kwh/l)

nodes.label: Coupled Peltier-Heat-Sink Operating Point (T_h ~50 C)
nodes.rationale: T_h is not a free parameter: T_h = T_amb + theta_sa*Q_h gives ~50 C (not ~35 C), lowering COP to ~0.28 and raising SEC; the claimed 0.5 K/W heat-sink resistance is 2-4x optimistic versus 50 mm extrusion datasheets (1.5-3 K/W).

nodes.label: Scale B Battery Sizing vs BOM Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Computed requirement C_batt >= 2,420 Wh vs BOM 1,800 Wh LiFePO4 pack (25% undersized); BOM price $180 is below the 350-600 USD market range, pushing realistic Scale B total to ~900 USD and payback to ~13 years.
nodes.norm_label: scale b battery sizing vs bom mismatch

nodes.label: Scale C Fleet Decomposition Recommendation
nodes.rationale: A 1.67-tonne water reservoir on a mobile gantry is structurally demanding and rare in O&M practice; decomposing Scale C into >=4 Scale-B-class units aligns with the pivot toward modular, scale-replicable robots.

nodes.rationale: At utility scale TEC is only conditionally sufficient (needs SEC <= 0.42 kWh/kg to match VCR, vs documented 2-12 kWh/kg); at robot scale the comparison inverts because a VCR compressor loop is too heavy and maintenance-bound for a 6 kg mobile platform.

nodes.label: Vapor-Compression Refrigeration (VCR) Condensation AWH
nodes.rationale: SEC 0.42 kWh/kg; the only route both mathematically sufficient and engineering-practical for the Benban duty (1.81 MW at 24 h or 3.61 MW in a 12 h night window for a 200 MW block); selected utility build path with drawings D-101 to D-107.

nodes.label: Levelised Cost of Water (LCOW)
nodes.rationale: Benban-era screening: VCR 13.98 USD/m3, absorption 13.18 USD/m3, TEC 44.96-244.96 USD/m3 depending on assumed SEC.

nodes.label: Smart Night-Only Harvesting Strategy (5 K Condensation Margin)
nodes.rationale: Harvest only in hours when the plate can be held 5 K below dew point within Imax; raises mean COP from 0.78 to 1.44 and cuts specific energy consumption by 78% at the cost of 34% of the water; 5 K margin maximizes annual yield since water is the binding constraint.
nodes.norm_label: smart night-only harvesting strategy (5 k condensation margin)

nodes.label: One Robot per Array Architecture
nodes.rationale: Full water self-sufficiency at 1 L/day costs 5.32 kWh/day and 5.34 m2 of dedicated PV, but a cleaned 2 m2 panel makes only ~2 kWh/day, so a self-powered one-robot-per-panel loop is infeasible; a high panel-to-robot ratio amortises the 1147 Wp supply and AWG hardware.

nodes.label: Seasonal Reservoir Storage of Harvested Water
nodes.rationale: Yield concentrates October-March (peak 4.5 L/day in November) and collapses June-September when dew points sit near 6 C at very low humidity; banking the winter surplus carries cleaning through the dead season, making AWG water a seasonal supplementary source, not on-demand.
nodes.norm_label: seasonal reservoir storage of harvested water

nodes.label: June Testing Problem (Humidified-Enclosure Validation Strategy)

nodes.author: Rahma El Hamouly

nodes.label: TEC (Peltier) Atmospheric Water Harvesting
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the robot's water source despite SEC of 2-12 kWh/kg (vs VCR 0.42) because it matches the DC power architecture of a PV-battery system, has no moving parts or refrigerant, responds instantly to intermittent PV power, and scales down to sub-litre daily duties where no commercial VCR exists.

nodes.label: Autonomous PV Cleaning Robot
nodes.rationale: No commercially available autonomous cleaner integrates its own water supply; the robot harvests water overnight, self-charges from the panels it cleans, and reduces maintenance to filter changes every weeks-months.

nodes.label: Three Deployment Scales (A: 80 W street lamp, B: 10 kWp commercial rooftop, C: 200 kWp industrial)
nodes.rationale: A single robot geometry cannot serve all PV applications because orientation, tilt, frame structure, array footprint, and water demand (0.15 / 3.0 / 40 L per day) differ significantly across scales.
nodes.norm_label: three deployment scales (a: 80 w street lamp, b: 10 kwp commercial rooftop, c: 200 kwp industrial)

nodes.label: PV Dust Soiling in Egypt and MENA
nodes.rationale: Soiling losses of 0.3-2.0 %/day (15-40 % monthly), with khamsin storms costing 5-10 % in a single day, motivate regular wet cleaning; economically optimal cleaning interval is 7-21 days.
nodes.norm_label: pv dust soiling in egypt and mena

nodes.label: Benban as Worst-Case Climate Validation Reference
nodes.rationale: Benban is not the deployment target; its arid microclimate (low RH, high ambient, large diurnal swing) is the most thermodynamically demanding case for a TEC condenser - adequate yield there guarantees performance in milder coastal/Delta new cities.
nodes.norm_label: benban as worst-case climate validation reference

nodes.label: ACWA Power Kom Ombo PV (200 MW AC, Aswan)
nodes.norm_label: acwa power kom ombo pv (200 mw ac, aswan)

nodes.label: EgyptERA (Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency)
nodes.norm_label: egyptera (egyptian electric utility and consumer protection regulatory agency)

nodes.label: AWH Minimum Practical Scale (Scaling Floor)
nodes.rationale: A VCR dehumidifier needs a compressor, refrigerant charge, and coils; below ~100 W cooling capacity fixed costs dominate and efficiency collapses, so commercial AWGs start at ~10-20 L/day. TEC tiles scale from ~1 W, so TEC's scaling floor is effectively zero - one $5 module yields ~100 mL/day, enough for a street-lamp cleaning cycle.

nodes.label: TEC-vs-VCR LCOW Breakeven Water Duty (~1.7-3.4 L/day)
nodes.rationale: The SEC-dominated LCOW term is scale-independent while the CAPEX term scales as 1/V_year; below roughly 1.7-3.4 L/day the smallest viable VCR's CAPEX is never amortised, so TEC has lower LCOW despite worse SEC. Street-lamp PV and much of residential rooftop sit on the TEC-preferred side; industrial and utility PV sit firmly on the VCR side.
nodes.norm_label: tec-vs-vcr lcow breakeven water duty (~1.7-3.4 l/day)

nodes.label: Cleaning Water Demand Model (V_year = w A N_clean (1+f_margin))
nodes.rationale: With w=1.8 L/m2/event, N_clean=18/yr, f_margin=0.25 and a 200 MW block (9.3e5 m2), annual demand is 3.77e4 m3/yr (~103,200 kg/day); parameters live in project_inputs.yaml as the single source of truth.
nodes.norm_label: cleaning water demand model (v_year = w a n_clean (1+f_margin))

nodes.label: Specific Energy Consumption (SEC_el = E_el / m_w, kWh/kg)
nodes.rationale: Single shared metric so all AWH families are compared on the same water mass; literature anchors: absorption 0.38, cooling condensation 0.42, adsorption 1.16, TEC band 2.0/6.0/12.0 kWh/kg.
nodes.norm_label: specific energy consumption (sec_el = e_el / m_w, kwh/kg)

nodes.label: Levelized Cost of Water (LCOW)
nodes.rationale: LCOW = CRF*CAPEX/V_year + rho*pi*SEC + O&M/V_year; separates a CAPEX-dominated term (scales 1/A) from an SEC-dominated term (scale-independent), which is what makes the technology ranking flip with PV asset size.

nodes.label: Vapor-Compression Refrigeration (VCR) Atmospheric Water Generator
nodes.rationale: Mature AWG family with the best kWh-per-kg among electrically driven condensers; wins at Benban scale (LCOW ~22.4 vs TEC ~85 USD/m3) but requires inverter AC, refrigerant handling, and compressor overhaul at 5-10 years.

nodes.label: PV Rinse Water Quality Targets (TDS, hardness, pH, particles)
nodes.rationale: Wet cleaning is spotting-sensitive: dissolved salts leave residues, so final rinse targets low hundreds of mg/L TDS or below (~50-100 mg/L with RO/demineralisation), near-neutral pH for frame/seal compatibility, and filtration to avoid scratching.
nodes.norm_label: pv rinse water quality targets (tds, hardness, ph, particles)

nodes.label: MOF Sorption AWH (advanced sorbents for low RH)
nodes.norm_label: mof sorption awh (advanced sorbents for low rh)

nodes.label: Diurnal Psychrometric Cycle Dominance in Desert AWH Sizing
nodes.rationale: Average RH misleads AWH sizing in deserts: midday is hot/dry while night and morning offer better condensation windows, so design must use hourly psychrometrics, not monthly RH means.
nodes.norm_label: diurnal psychrometric cycle dominance in desert awh sizing

nodes.label: AWH-Centric Scope Split (cleaner as black box)
nodes.rationale: Full mechatronics design is optional: the thesis can define the cleaning interface (peak flow, pressure, water-quality limits, connection point) and treat the cleaning robot as a black box, keeping AWH sizing, treatment, and energy scheduling in scope.
nodes.norm_label: awh-centric scope split (cleaner as black box)

nodes.label: Phased Methodology A-E (plant class, weather/soiling, water demand, AWH screening, integrated simulation)
nodes.norm_label: phased methodology a-e (plant class, weather/soiling, water demand, awh screening, integrated simulation)

nodes.label: PVsyst PV Simulation Tool (monthly soiling loss factors)
nodes.norm_label: pvsyst pv simulation tool (monthly soiling loss factors)

nodes.label: TEC Governing Equations (Qc, Pin, COP; design point Tc=14C, Th=58C, COP=0.38)
nodes.rationale: First-principles Peltier model (alpha=0.0534 V/K, R=1.98 ohm, K=0.524 W/K) sizes condensate yield (~0.026 L/h per module) and module counts per scale, validated against published experimental TEC AWG data.
nodes.norm_label: tec governing equations (qc, pin, cop; design point tc=14c, th=58c, cop=0.38)

nodes.label: TEC1-12706 Peltier Module (12 V, 6 A, 72 W max)
nodes.rationale: Selected for Egyptian-market availability and low cost; commodity single-stage module that can be stacked or paralleled trivially.
nodes.norm_label: tec1-12706 peltier module (12 v, 6 a, 72 w max)

nodes.label: Sub-Cooling Condensation Margin Design Point (5 K)
nodes.rationale: The 5 K margin below dew point sits at the per-tile water-yield maximum: smaller margins fail to condense reliably, larger margins waste COP; SEC flattens near 4 kWh/L between 5-8 K.
nodes.norm_label: sub-cooling condensation margin design point (5 k)

nodes.label: Four-State Supervisory Control (Harvest, Standby, Clean, Emergency)
nodes.rationale: ESP32-class microcontroller with RTC scheduling and sensor feedback enables unsupervised operation - the defining requirement of the autonomous robot.
nodes.norm_label: four-state supervisory control (harvest, standby, clean, emergency)

nodes.label: Daily Energy Budget (TEC stack ~79% of demand)
nodes.rationale: AWG cooling, not mobility or cleaning, dominates the power design; this drives PV self-consumption sizing and battery capacity.
nodes.norm_label: daily energy budget (tec stack ~79% of demand)

nodes.label: 10 L/day as Per-Unit TEC AWG Rating at Nominal Psychrometric Conditions
nodes.rationale: Per-unit output is fixed in hardware by three constraints: Peltier cold-side duty ceiling, fan airflow capacity, and condenser surface area; manufacturers scale capacity by replicating units, not building monolithic larger ones. Clarifying per-unit vs aggregate changes the Benban deployment count by four orders of magnitude (10,322 units nominal).
nodes.norm_label: 10 l/day as per-unit tec awg rating at nominal psychrometric conditions

nodes.label: Architecture A - Single High-Capacity Monolithic TEC Assembly
nodes.rationale: Conceptual extreme only: no commercial continuous TEC product line exists between 10 L/day and 100,000 L/day.
nodes.norm_label: architecture a - single high-capacity monolithic tec assembly

nodes.label: Architecture B - Multi-Unit Parallel TEC Deployment (N units, N+1 redundancy)
nodes.rationale: The architecture industry actually implements: catalogue units manifolded into a common water plenum; single-tile failure degrades output marginally rather than catastrophically.
nodes.norm_label: architecture b - multi-unit parallel tec deployment (n units, n+1 redundancy)

nodes.label: Psychrometric Derating Factor (eta_derate ~ 0.36 at Benban)
nodes.rationale: Nameplate ratings assume 27C / 60% RH (13.33 g/kg); Benban's annual-mean humidity ratio of 4.844 g/kg derates a nominal 10 L/day unit to ~3.6 L/day (2.79 L/day in the driest month).

nodes.label: Egyptian Electricity Tariff Structure (EgyptERA tiered, Aug 2024 revision)
nodes.rationale: Tiered residential/commercial and flat industrial tariffs plus EGP 48/USD exchange rate, 5% customs and 14% VAT on HS 8415 hardware materially shift the v1.0 global LCOW model; TEC LCOW for distributed tiers improves ~25-35% with Egypt-market inputs while the Benban utility conclusion is unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: egyptian electricity tariff structure (egyptera tiered, aug 2024 revision)

nodes.label: PV-Clipped Self-Consumption Energy Sourcing
nodes.rationale: Midday rooftop PV is often curtailed by inverter clipping or excess self-consumption, so an AWG operating during the PV peak incurs near-zero marginal electricity cost - further improving distributed TEC economics; not captured by constant-tariff models.

nodes.label: Carnot COP Ceiling and Second-Law Efficiency (COP_Carnot ~ 13 at Benban operating point)
nodes.rationale: The Carnot ceiling is a function of state, not device, so it is identical for TEC and VCR; the gap is in second-law efficiency: TEC 2.3-3.8% vs VCR 19-42% at the same temperature lift.
nodes.norm_label: carnot cop ceiling and second-law efficiency (cop_carnot ~ 13 at benban operating point)

nodes.label: Thermoelectric Figure of Merit ZT (Bi2Te3 ~ 1.0)
nodes.rationale: Commercial Bi2Te3 modules have ZT ~ 1.0, ceiling practical COP near 0.6-0.7 at small dT; emerging ZT->2 materials are not commercially available, so TEC's efficiency disadvantage is structural, not a manufacturing-maturity issue.

nodes.label: Refrigerant GWP Liability of VCR (R-410A GWP 2088)
nodes.rationale: A single 3 kg R-410A charge equals 6264 kg CO2e (~14 MWh of Egyptian grid electricity); TEC uses no refrigerant, giving zero fugitive-GWP emissions and ~70% lower operational GHG when PV-powered, but VCR's 3-6x lower SEC outweighs this at grid emission factors above ~0.1 kgCO2e/kWh.
nodes.norm_label: refrigerant gwp liability of vcr (r-410a gwp 2088)

nodes.label: Tellurium Supply Criticality (global supply ~580 t/yr)
nodes.rationale: TEC's only material-level sustainability liability: USGS lists Te among critical minerals and Egypt would import 100% of Peltier modules.

nodes.label: Passive AWH Materials (structured surfaces, MOFs, hygroscopic compounds, functional hydrogels)
nodes.rationale: Cheap, zero secondary-energy, easy-install alternatives to electricity-driven dew collection and desalination; challenged by low capacity at low humidity, self-desorption, and weak solar-thermal conversion.
nodes.norm_label: passive awh materials (structured surfaces, mofs, hygroscopic compounds, functional hydrogels)

nodes.norm_label: saturated (fog) water harvesting via biomimetic surfaces

nodes.norm_label: moisture sorption mechanisms (absorption vs adsorption; langmuir/bet isotherms)

nodes.label: Materials-Enabled Moisture Harvesting (water affinity instead of cooling-driven local RH)

nodes.norm_label: materials-enabled moisture harvesting (water affinity instead of cooling-driven local rh)
